causal_claim.trigger: Commit S2 is deployed to the payment service at 16:58:19Z, after which payment error calls rise from 0 to 1.
causal_claim.defect: In validateCard (src/payment/card.js, line 12) the card type is compared case-sensitively against the literals 'VISA' and 'MasterCard', so the lowercase 'visa' card type observed in the trace fails validation.
causal_claim.failure: Every valid Visa charge is rejected with 'Sorry, we cannot process visa credit cards. Only VISA or MasterCard is accepted.' and the payment span ends in STATUS_CODE_ERROR, causing the 'every valid charge fails' incident.

predicted_observations.statement: Payment error count is 0 in the window ending at the S2 deployment and rises to 1 immediately after.
The failing trace has card_type 'visa' and card_valid:true yet ends in STATUS_CODE_ERROR.
The log text reveals the case mismatch: valid 'visa' is rejected while the accepted set is literally 'VISA' or 'MasterCard'.
The 'cannot process' rejection is located in validateCard at card.js:12.

alternatives: paymentUnreachable feature flag being true causing failures

proposed_tests.procedure: Normalize card type casing (toLowerCase) before comparison in validateCard and re-run the charge driver; observe if the valid visa charge then succeeds.
proposed_tests.bounds: Unit scope in payment service validateCard; demo environment; no production writes.
permissions: read access to the charge driver in the demo environment

expected.this_hypothesis: the charge span for a valid visa card returns STATUS_CODE_OK after normalization

proposed_tests.procedure: Toggle paymentUnreachable flag to false and re-run the charge driver while leaving the card type with lowercase 'visa'.
permissions: flagd write access for demo environment

expected.this_hypothesis: the charge still fails with the card-type validation error, confirming the flag is not the root cause

causal_claim.trigger: A feature flag query returns paymentUnreachable=true at the failure window.
causal_claim.defect: The paymentUnreachable flag could be configured to make the payment backend appear unreachable, presenting as charge errors.
causal_claim.failure: Charges fail as an unreachability/connectivity error on the payment service.

predicted_observations.statement: The flagd query returns paymentUnreachable=true at the failure window.

proposed_tests.procedure: Set paymentUnreachable=false and observe whether the charge succeeds.
permissions: flagd write access for demo environment

expected.this_hypothesis: the charge still fails with the card-type validation error, indicating the flag is not the root cause

stated_objections.statement: The paymentUnreachable flag (H2) is weakly supported: the failing trace reaches validateCard and emits a semantic card-type validation error with card_valid:true, inconsistent with an unreachable-backend failure mode.
The paymentFailure flag is 0, so a deliberate payment-failure chaos injection is not active and cannot be cited as the root cause.
The failure is fully explained by the case-sensitive comparison in code, with the error rate changing only after the S2 deployment, so no external or flag-driven cause is required.
